subject: Post-call: security & vendor roster — clarify data boundaries
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Amit Shah <amit.shah@brightwavehealth.com>, Tanya Lopez <tanya.lopez@brightwavehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-10-17T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: security & vendor roster — clarify data boundaries

Hi Amit / Tanya,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on the security/compliance items you flagged.

Key takeaways from the call:
- Primary concerns: SOC 2 attestation status, HIPAA handling for PHI pipelines, and GDPR data residency for EU-subject records.
- Scope note: BrightWave will only send tokenized patient identifiers and selected metadata to Redwood for inference; sensitive raw files (full PHI documents) will remain in your environment for now.
- Integration pattern: you are evaluating Hosted API first, with Dedicated/Private as options if additional isolation or KMS control is required.

Immediate asks we agreed on:
1) We will share our current third-party roster (subprocessors) with role-level access and data boundaries.
2) Provide SOC 2 summary and expected timeline for the next Type II cycle.
3) Clarify encryption (in transit and at rest) and whether any subprocessors have access to unredacted PII.
4) Initiate the security questionnaire (we can push a vendor questionnaire link to your security inbox).

What I'll do by EOD tomorrow: attach the vendor roster CSV and a short data handoff matrix that maps which Redwood components touch which data types.

Would you confirm whether BrightWave needs a signed DPA before we share the roster, or if an NDA/DPA is already in place with procurement?

Thanks —

Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0183

Subject: Re: Post-call: security & vendor roster — clarify data boundaries

Jordan —

Thanks for the recap, helpful. A couple of clarifying questions before we circulate internally to engineering/security: 

- SOC 2: do you have a current Type II report from the past 12 months? If not, what is the audit cadence and expected completion for the current engagement?
- Subprocessors: we need a short roster with the role (compute, storage, logging), the provider (AWS/GCP/etc.), and the region(s) where data is processed/stored. Can you flag any subprocessor that has the ability to access unredacted PHI?
- Encryption & KMS: confirm default key management (Redwood-managed KMS) and whether customer-managed keys (BYOK) are available on Dedicated/Private. Also confirm TLS versions in use and at-rest encryption cipher.
- Questionnaire: yes, please push the vendor questionnaire link to security@brightwavehealth.com — they prefer a pre-filled roster so they can skip some items.

We also need to understand retention: if BrightWave requests deletion of inference logs for a particular tenant, what is the SLA and process?

No DPA required to share a redacted roster (provider + role + region), but we will need a DPA before a full subprocessor contract is signed.

Amit
Head of Security Ops
BrightWave Health

Subject: Re: Post-call: security & vendor roster — clarify data boundaries

Hi Amit / Tanya —

Following up with the items Jordan promised. Attached: redwood_vendor_roster_2028-10.csv (role, provider, region, minimal access notes), SOC2_summary_2028.pdf (one-page status + control highlights), and data_handoff_matrix_2028.xlsx (example mappings).

Quick answers inline to your bullets: 
- SOC 2: Redwood completed SOC 2 Type II for the audit period Jan–Dec 2027; the Type II engagement for 2028 is in progress with fieldwork completed in Sept 2028 and the final report expected by Nov 30, 2028. The one-page summary highlights scope and exclusions.
- Subprocessors (summary):
  * AWS (compute + storage) — us-west-2, us-east-1 — hosts serving runtime (token cache, model inference).
  * Google Cloud (BigQuery / analytics) — us-central1 — aggregated telemetry and cost analytics (no raw tokens).
  * S3-compatible backups on AWS GovCloud (for select customers opting into Dedicated) — gov-west-1 — only activated on a per-customer basis.
  * Redis / managed caching providers — eu-west-1 for EU tenants (cache entries are truncated token prefixes; full-session KV is encrypted).
  * Logging/observability (Datadog) — us-east-1 — traces and anonymized metrics; raw user content is redacted before forwarding.

- Access to unredacted PHI: by default, Redwood does not persist raw unredacted PHI in hosted deployments; where customers route raw PHI (rare), that is done in Dedicated/Private or via direct connectors under a customer-managed bucket — and those configurations are explicitly documented in the data_handoff_matrix. Any customer who needs us to process raw PHI signs an additional data processing addendum and we put tighter controls (restricted operator access, dedicated vaults).

- Encryption/KMS:
  * In transit: TLS 1.3 (mutual TLS available for Dedicated/private peering).
  * At rest: AES-256.
  * KMS: Redwood-managed keys by default (AWS KMS / GCP KMS). Customer-managed keys (BYOK) are available for Dedicated and Private deployments; we also offer HSM integrations for on-prem.

- Deletion SLA: For hosted customers we have a documented retention/erase process; deletion requests are processed within 72 hours and a confirmation is provided. For Dedicated/Private, retention policies are controlled per the contract. See the attached data_handoff_matrix for record-level retention patterns.

Next steps we propose:
1) We will push the vendor questionnaire link to security@brightwavehealth.com now (you should receive an invite with pre-populated roster fields).
2) If you confirm the need, we can schedule a short security deep-dive next week (30 min) with our infra/security lead to walk the data flow diagram.

Let us know which slots next week work for you and whether you want the roster redacted (provider + role only) or full contact details.

Thanks,

Karthik Iyer
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai | +1 650-555-0199
